correctness.rationale: For an input with s original runs the channel removes exactly s−1 symbols and its output has at most s runs; this gives n>=m+r−1. Canonical extension of every noninitial output run by one symbol gives the unique inverse at equality. Appending disappearing singleton runs proves reachability at every larger n. q(q−1)^(r−1) binomial(m−1,r−1) counts outputs with m symbols and r runs; summing gives exact image size and a matching zero-error code. The rational GF and dominant root follow algebraically. Standalone exhaustive and integer checks agree.

Conversely, our threshold-one result does not improve or contradict the existing higher-threshold results. The finite-block identity and preimage uniqueness require a specific structural argument not contained in the compared published statements.

evidence: The channel is a deterministic run-boundary deletion transducer: it keeps every symbol that is equal to its predecessor, plus the initial symbol. The original paper defines contextual deletion at the first symbol following a completed sufficiently long run (Definitions 1 and 3).
No exact threshold-one output-enumeration theorem was found in the inspected primary material or exact-transducer searches.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Alternative terminology includes run-boundary suppression, start-of-run deletion, maximal-run contraction and deterministic contextual deletion. The image-count identity is stronger than any general qualitative channel bound and cannot be inferred from a coincident Fibonacci sequence or a constrained-language capacity without a channel-image equivalence. No such equivalence was found in inspected sources.
